title: Operator-visible degradation modes and client notification contracts for serving PRD
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Following the region outage postmortem we observed multiple customer applications experiencing silent quality degradations without clear signals that the platform had entered a lowered-capacity operating mode. This ticket updates the serving PRD to define operator-visible deterministic degradation modes, the client-facing notification contracts (API headers, error types, and console alerts), and acceptance criteria so downstream teams and customers can detect and adapt to degradations predictably.

Goals:
- Define clear, finite degradation modes (e.g., reduced-concurrency, affinity-limited, graceful-shed) with deterministic semantics for latency, quality, and retry behavior.
- Specify operator controls and rollout semantics (canary to region, immediate manual trigger, automated entry via SLO gates).
- Add client-visible contracts: response headers, structured error codes, and documented SDK behavior to enable deterministic client fallbacks.
- Ensure observability: per-mode dashboards, alerts, and synthetic checks.
- Codify acceptance tests, runbook updates, and release gating so the feature is verifiable in staging and production.

Scope clarifications (what this PRD change will and will not cover):
- In scope: PRD requirements and acceptance criteria for the serving control plane and API surface; console notifications and telemetry naming conventions; automated SLO-triggered mode entry rules and tests.
- Out of scope: low-level kernel scheduling optimizations, per-model quantization recommendations, or customer SDK shipping (SDK changes will be tracked separately once API contract is finalized).

Rationale: The postmortem identified three failure modes where serving capacity dropped and customers saw lower-quality responses without explicit signals to back off or switch models. Engineering can implement numerous fallback strategies, but without a deterministic, observable contract customers can't safely adapt. This PRD update aligns product expectations with operator behavior and provides a clear signal path for customers and platform automation.
acceptance_criteria: Define and document at least three named degradation modes with precise semantics for throughput, per-request latency targets, token-quality expectations, and allowable batching differences.

API contract: server responses include 'X-Redwood-Degraded: <mode>' header when any degradation mode is active; documented structured error code 'RDW_DEGRADED' for cases where requests are rejected due to mode rules.
Console: tenant-level banner and a per-tenant 'degradation mode' timeline in the Console UI; ability for operators to annotate mode entries with reason and incident link.

SLO gating: automated trigger rules expressed in PRD that transition serving to a degradation mode when 95th-percentile token latency exceeds configured threshold for the affected region for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows.

Observability: new dashboards (latency by mode, headroom by queue depth, synthetic QA pass rate by model) and at least 5 alerts mapped to runbook steps; dashboards have stable IDs and are linked from the PRD.
Client compatibility: document SDK guidance for graceful fallback when 'X-Redwood-Degraded' is present (recommended backoff, retry windows, and model pinning strategies).

E2E tests: staging harness includes a degradation-mode simulator that can force each named mode and verify headers, console banners, dashboard signals, and behavior of an example client app under each mode.
Runbooks: updated runbook for each degradation mode including operator playbook for escalation, verification, and rollback; runbooks linked in PRD and referenced in acceptance tests.
Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime-1.20 release flag with a canary rollout strategy for 5% of traffic in two regions before global enablement; rollback criteria defined in PRD.
